text:
Dear Partners,

We write this quarter the way a farmer writes to his neighbors after the first hard frost of the season — plainly, and without pretending the weather was kinder than it was. Equities have entered bear market territory, public spreads have gapped wider on default fears, and the tape has been unforgiving to anyone marked to it daily. We are not immune to the weather. We are, however, built for it.

Stonebeck's reported return this quarter was -8.5%, bringing our year-to-date figure to -12.0%. We will not dress that up. Since inception, our partnership with you has returned +10.0%, and that number matters more to us than any single quarter's turbulence, because we did not build this book to sprint — we built it to last.

We know some of you will look at public equities down -18.0% for the quarter and ask why our marks did not fall as far, or conversely, why they fell at all if credit sits senior in the structure. Both questions deserve an honest answer. Our positions benefit from structural seniority — that remains the case today — but seniority does not mean immunity to marks; our NAV index sits at 88.0, reflecting the same market stress working its way through spreads, now at 780bps, wider than we'd like to see. We are not going to pretend a widening market doesn't touch our book. We think the gap between our result and the equity market's result reflects the protections we structured in at origination, not a delay in recognizing reality.

On the covenant side, we continue the constructive amendment conversations we described last quarter. These are not adversarial proceedings — they are what partnership looks like when a borrower hits a rough patch and both sides would rather work it out than force a fire sale. Our sponsor relationships remain at the table, which we take as a good sign.

The macro backdrop is not making anyone's job easier. Policy rate sits at 5.25% against inflation running 4.1%, a combination that keeps refinancing conversations tense and borrowers' cash flows tight. We are watching this closely. Should conditions deteriorate further, we would expect more amendment activity before we would expect impairment — but we hold that view with appropriate humility, not certainty.

We think patience remains the right posture. We think our seniority remains real. We also think it would be foolish to promise you calm seas simply because we've navigated rough ones before. This cycle may test structures that have not been tested at this scale, and prudent investors — which is what you are — should expect more volatility in the marks before things settle. There remains a risk that conditions worsen further before they improve, and we will continue to watch that closely.

We remain grateful for your trust, and we remain in this with you.

With respect,
Stonebeck Credit
